question: So when exactly is the first half of the property tax due, before it counts as late?
expected_answer: The first half-year instalment is due by 31 July under the 2026-27 schedule.

key_facts: first half-year instalment is due by 31 July
meta.note: Superseded 2024-26 schedule says 30 June; retrieval must pick the current one.

question: Will I get a few percent off if I pay the whole year's property tax up front?
expected_answer: There's no discount for that any more: the early payment rebate was withdrawn from 2026-27, so paying the full year in advance gets no rebate.

key_facts: early payment rebate has been withdrawn
no rebate is given for paying the full year in advance
meta.note: Common norm: Indian municipal corporations give a 5 to 10 percent rebate for paying the full year early (and this corporation's superseded schedule gave 10 percent).

question: I'm renting our flat out this year, so who would pay the property tax, me or the tenant?
expected_answer: The owner is legally liable for property tax; a tenant pays only if the rent agreement says so, and even then the owner remains answerable to the municipality.

question: I'm two months late on about forty thousand rupees of tax, so what percent penalty is that?
expected_answer: The penalty is 2 percent per month or part of a month, so two months late is 4 percent, about ₹1,600 on ₹40,000.

key_facts: 2 percent per month or part of a month
meta.note: Superseded schedule says 1.5 percent per month.

question: Our home's locked up and empty all year, but is it taxed the same as an occupied one?
expected_answer: Yes, in full: there's no vacancy remission now, so a locked or empty building is taxed in full, as the remission for vacant buildings was discontinued in 2026-27.

meta.note: Common norm: Indian municipal laws allow a vacancy remission on property tax for empty buildings (the superseded schedule gave 50 percent).

question: Now that I've paid stamp duty on the flat, do I still owe you property tax each year?
expected_answer: Yes. Stamp duty is a one-time state tax paid on registering the purchase, while property tax is a separate recurring tax paid to the municipality every year for owning the property.

question: If the survey finds, um, my flat's bigger than I declared, what penalty should I expect?
expected_answer: If the surveyed carpet area is more than 5 percent above what you declared, you pay the tax difference for up to the previous 3 years plus a penalty of twice the difference for the current year.

key_facts: twice the difference for the current year

question: It's the area part, what's the rule on counting the outer walls in my carpet area?
expected_answer: No, carpet area is the net usable floor area inside the walls, so the thickness of the external walls is left out.

history.content: Hi, I'm filling in the self-assessment form for our new flat.
Sure, I can help with that. Which part of the form are you on?

question: She's about five weeks old, can I still register her at the ward office?
expected_answer: Yes, but as it's past 30 days you need to pay a late fee of ₹75, give an affidavit on plain paper and get written permission from the zonal registrar at the zone office on a Tuesday or Friday.

history.content: Hi, I need to register my daughter's birth, she was born at home.
Congratulations! How old is she now?

meta.note: Generic answer (yes, with a small late fee and an affidavit) is plausible but misses the fee and the zone office permission step.

question: I need, like, five extra copies of my dad's death certificate, what will that come to?
expected_answer: Additional copies cost ₹50 each, so five copies would be ₹250, ready in 3 working days.

meta.note: Marriage doc lists ₹100 per certified copy (distractor).

question: Will the bank ask for my dad's death certificate before they move his account to my mum?
expected_answer: Yes, the bank will ask for a copy of the death certificate, along with the nominee's or legal heir's claim form and ID, before it settles or transfers the account.

question: Does a shop's trade licence need renewing every year, and by what date?
expected_answer: No, trade licences are now issued for a block of three financial years with no annual renewal; you apply for the next block at least 30 days before it expires.

meta.note: Common norm: municipal trade licences in India are renewed every year by 31 March.

question: My trade licence ran out about two months ago, so is there a penalty, and what percent?
expected_answer: Yes: it's 25 percent of the licence fee for each quarter or part of a quarter, so 25 percent for two months.

key_facts: 25 percent of the fee for each quarter or part of a quarter

question: I've got GST registration for the shop, so do I still pay for your trade licence?
expected_answer: Yes. GST registration is a tax registration and doesn't replace the municipal trade licence, which is a separate permission to run the business at those premises.

question: So how long will it take to get a building plan approved for a small ground plus one house?
expected_answer: On a plot up to 300 square metres it can go through self-certification by a registered architect, with approval issued within 7 working days; otherwise it's within 30 working days after a site inspection.

meta.note: Generic answer (one to two months) is plausible for the regular route but misses the 7-day self-certification route.

question: How much is one square metre in square feet, roughly, as I need to get my plot size?
expected_answer: One square metre is about 10.76 square feet.

question: How much is it to get a new half inch water connection we need for our house?
expected_answer: A 15 mm (half inch) domestic connection costs ₹4,200 including the meter, plus any road restoration charge if a road has to be cut.

question: We need our house connected to the city sewer line, but is there a fee for that?
expected_answer: Yes, a domestic sewer connection is a fixed ₹2,800 per property.

question: How long should we, um, let the tap run if the water's muddy after a repair?
expected_answer: Run the cold tap for a few minutes until the water runs clear, and don't drink it until then; boil it if you're unsure.

question: Will the garbage van take my dry waste every morning, um, along with the wet stuff?
expected_answer: No, dry waste is collected only on Wednesdays and Saturdays; only wet waste is collected every day.

meta.note: Common norm: door-to-door collection takes segregated wet and dry waste together every day.

question: We need someone to, like, come and pick up our old sofa, but is that free?
expected_answer: Yes, as long as it's one of your two free bulk pickups for the financial year (up to one cubic metre each); book at least 48 hours ahead.

key_facts: two free bulk pickups per financial year
meta.note: Common norm: municipal bulky waste collection is a paid service.

question: When I'm sorting the dry waste, what do I do with used sanitary pads?
expected_answer: Keep them out of the dry waste: wrap them in newspaper or a paper bag and hand them over separately as sanitary waste.

question: Is registration only for dogs, or does my cat have to be registered too?
expected_answer: Cats must be registered too: every pet cat needs registration at ₹150 a year, renewed by 30 April.

meta.note: Common norm: Indian municipalities require registration for pet dogs only, not cats.

question: It's a dog we bought from a breeder, so what's the registration fee each year?
expected_answer: It's ₹500 per year for each dog, renewed every year by 30 April.

history.content: Hi, I wanted to ask about registering a pet we just got.
Sure. Is it a dog or a cat, and was it adopted or bought?

question: How often does my dog have to get a rabies shot, once a year?
expected_answer: After the first dose at about three months and a booster, it needs a rabies booster every year.

question: There's a big tree in our compound we need cut down, how much is the deposit in rupees?
expected_answer: You need permission, with a ₹200 application fee and a refundable deposit of ₹5,000 per tree, returned once three saplings per tree have survived a year.

question: For the branches touching the power lines by our gate, should I cut those myself?
expected_answer: No, don't touch branches near live lines; ask the electricity company to switch off or trim them, since a branch can conduct current.

question: How long do you guys usually take to fix a streetlight once I've complained?
expected_answer: A streetlight that's not working is repaired within 72 hours; if not, the complaint escalates automatically to the ward's assistant commissioner.

meta.note: Generic answer (a few days, or 48 hours) is plausible but imprecise.

question: Will the ward office take my tax in cash on a Saturday afternoon, or is it shut?
expected_answer: No, on Saturdays ward offices are only open 10 am to 1:30 pm with cash counters closing at 1 pm, and they're shut on the second and fourth Saturdays.

question: Sure, for the report, how much detail is enough for the crew to find the spot?
expected_answer: Give the exact location with the road name and a nearby landmark, the rough size of the pothole, and a photo if you can.

history.content: Hi, there's a huge pothole near the end of our lane.
Sorry about that, I can raise a complaint for you right now.
